title: EXP-062 — Hello World Part 4 Section 4: Configure Picture Import UI on User-Scope FX_Items Form
objective: Using only the existing authenticated Mongoose Web Designer, open the exact User-scoped FX_Items Form and capture its complete pre-change component, binding, geometry, variable, and event-handler baseline. Follow hello-world-pt4.md Section 4 (03:00–05:13). Delete exactly the FX_VarTestEdit component while preserving its associated FX_VarTest variable and the existing FX_Test handler group. Retain the FX_RefreshButton Name, create the FX_sImport caption string with literal text Import through the documented Caption ellipsis workflow, and assign that string to the button. Add exactly one Static component named FX_PictureStatic to the right of the existing input fields, bind it to the FX_Picture IDO property, and set No Colon to True. Create one custom event FX_ImportPicture with a Binary Value Action configured for Action Type Import and component FX_PictureStatic. Assign FX_ImportPicture to FX_RefreshButton Events > Primary, replacing the previous FX_Test assignment without deleting FX_Test or its two actions. Verify every intended change and all preserved baseline properties before performing exactly one ordinary Designer Save. Close and reopen the same User-scoped Form, verify complete definition recovery, and inspect the runtime Form read-only for the three original records, Import button, and empty picture Static. Do not activate the Import action. Capture decisive native UI evidence and classify successful findings as observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt4.md Section 4 at 03:00–05:13, and relevant EXP-045, EXP-050, EXP-051, EXP-054-R2, EXP-056, EXP-057, EXP-058, and EXP-061 evidence before browser interaction.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-062-hello-world-part-4-section-4-configure-picture-import-ui.md and evidence/EXP-062/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the operator-provided repository baseline, pre-existing changes, worker-written-file inventory, and cumulative browser action audit.
Use the existing authenticated Designer session without deliberate reauthentication, browser refresh, restart, or configuration change.

Confirm editing permission and editing scope User. Verify the loaded FX_Items Form definition identity by Form Name, ScopeType User, and ScopeName matching the authenticated operator. Never edit Site Default or another version.
Establish that the Designer is clean and responsive, with no authentication challenge, unexpected dialog, or unsaved changes before mutation.

Capture a complete baseline inventory of FX_Items Form components, including component Name, Type, parent/container, Caption, binding, Data Source Binding Type, geometry, relevant Miscellaneous attributes, event assignments, and other readable properties.
Record the complete properties of FX_VarTestEdit before deletion. Establish that exactly one such component exists and distinguish it from the separate FX_VarTest variable.
Capture the complete FX_RefreshButton baseline, including its Name, Caption, geometry, and current Events > Primary assignment.
Record the pre-change handler inventory, including the existing FX_Test group and both actions, and verify that FX_ImportPicture does not already exist.

Confirm that the FX_Picture property created in EXP-061 is available through the supported Designer binding selection surface. If it is missing, ambiguous, or unavailable, stop before saving and report the blocker.
Delete exactly one existing Form component, FX_VarTestEdit, using the supported Designer component-selection and deletion workflow. Verify that no other component was deleted.
Preserve the FX_VarTest variable definition and all existing FX_Test event-handler definitions and actions.
Retain the existing FX_RefreshButton component and its exact Name. Change its Caption using the existing caption-string lookup and creation workflow.

Create exactly one FX_sImport string if absent, through Caption ellipsis. When the native UI offers to create the missing string, approve only that exact FX_sImport creation. Replace any prefilled split value with literal Import, commit the text cell using Tab or Enter, and verify the committed value before confirming the dialog.
If FX_sImport already exists, inspect its current value and identity before making any change; stop for review if its status conflicts with the requested new-string creation.
Assign Caption string ID FX_sImport to FX_RefreshButton and verify the displayed Caption resolves to Import.
Preserve FX_RefreshButton geometry unless moving it is demonstrably necessary to make space for the picture Static. Any necessary movement must be measured, documented, and limited to that component.
Add exactly one Toolbox Static component named FX_PictureStatic to the right of the existing input fields, using the supported Designer placement controls.
Set FX_PictureStatic Data Source Binding Type to Property and Binding to FX_Picture through a supported native property-selection control. Require an unambiguous committed selection.

Set FX_PictureStatic Miscellaneous > Specific Attributes > No Colon to True, using its supported visible property control. If the attribute cannot be identified or verified, stop before Save rather than guessing.
Capture FX_PictureStatic component identity, type, parent, geometry, property binding, and No Colon value.
Within Details > Event Handlers, create exactly one new custom event named FX_ImportPicture. Enter the new name into the event combobox according to the previously observed EXP-058 procedure.

Configure FX_ImportPicture with Response Type Binary Value Action and its intended action parameters: Action Type Import and component FX_PictureStatic. Capture the exact native field names and selected values.

Set FX_RefreshButton Events > Primary to FX_ImportPicture. Verify the authoritative Primary property after committing the selection rather than relying on the potentially stale Components-grid Event to generate column.

Before Save, compare the complete edited Form against the recorded baseline. Require the five intended changes and no unauthorized changes to other components, variables, handlers, bindings, or layout.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after every mutation and configuration gate passes. Record the native Save response verbatim and confirm the Designer returns to a demonstrably clean state.
Re-read FX_VarTest, the FX_Test handler group with its two actions, FX_RefreshButton, FX_PictureStatic, FX_ImportPicture, and all other baseline components after Save.
Close the clean FX_Items Designer Form tab exactly once through its supported Form-tab close control, without an unsaved-changes prompt.

Reopen the exact FX_Items User-scoped Form once through the supported Designer recent-forms route. Permit at most one documented recent-forms retry, then the native Open > Select Form fallback if needed, recording the actual path. Never use an unsupported direct URL.

After reopening, verify the same Form Name, ScopeType User, and ScopeName, and compare all intended changes and all preserved components, variables, handlers, event assignments, geometry, and bindings against the pre-Save and original baselines.
Verify that the recovered Form is clean, with Designer Save disabled, and that the FX_Test group retains both original actions.

Open the existing FX_Items runtime Form once through a supported native route without altering inherited tabs. Verify three original business records, a visible Import button, an empty picture Static, no unexpected prompt, and a clean Save-disabled state.
Preserve all FX_Items business records. The Import button must not be activated during this experiment.
Leave the FX_Items IDO checkout owned by the existing operator, without performing checkout-management operations.

Capture screenshots and accessibility readbacks that identify the exact Form, editing scope, selected component or handler, relevant property values, Save result, recovered definition, and runtime outcome.

Record any blocker after no more than one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection for a failed locator or visibility inspection. Do not expand the procedure or retry uncertain mutations.

Classify successful findings as observed only and explicitly distinguish Form-definition recovery from independent database durability, cache behavior, binary storage, and runtime image-import functionality.

acceptance_checks.description: The required AGENTS.md, tutorial Section 4, and relevant prior experiment evidence were reviewed. The authenticated Designer is usable, no session challenge is present, and exactly the intended FX_Items User-scoped Form version is identified by Name, ScopeType, and ScopeName. Designer Save is initially disabled. Evidence: source-review notes, identity and scope screenshot, initial Designer screenshot, and action audit.

Before mutation, the complete FX_Items component baseline is captured with readable Name, Type, parent/container, Caption, binding, geometry, events, and relevant properties. Exactly one FX_VarTestEdit and one FX_RefreshButton are identified. The FX_VarTest variable and existing FX_Test handler group with two actions are recorded. FX_ImportPicture is absent, and the intended FX_Picture binding prerequisite is verified through supported native UI. Evidence: full component inventory, FX_VarTestEdit property screenshots, variable readback, handler/action inventory, binding evidence, and baseline matrix.

Exactly one component, FX_VarTestEdit, is deleted. Its previously recorded identity is no longer present in the component tree or inventory, component cardinality decreases by exactly one, and no other baseline component is removed. The FX_VarTest variable and FX_Test handler group remain. Evidence: before/after component inventories, deletion action audit, and variable/handler readbacks.

Exactly one FX_sImport caption string is created through the supported Caption ellipsis workflow, if the prerequisite absence gate passes. Its committed literal value is Import, and FX_RefreshButton retains its original Name while its Caption references FX_sImport and visibly resolves to Import. Its other properties and geometry remain unchanged unless a documented space requirement justifies a narrowly scoped movement. Evidence: native string-creation prompt and committed value, Caption-property readback, displayed button caption, baseline comparison, and action counts.

Exactly one new Static component named FX_PictureStatic is added to the right of the input fields. Its committed Data Source Binding Type is Property, its Binding is FX_Picture, and Miscellaneous > Specific Attributes > No Colon is visibly True. The selected component identity, parent, type, and geometry are recorded. Evidence: Designer layout screenshot, component-tree readback, binding selector, complete property-grid values, and component cardinality.

Exactly one new custom event FX_ImportPicture is present in Details > Event Handlers. It has one action with Response Type Binary Value Action and the exact action parameters Action Type Import and component FX_PictureStatic. The event name and every field are visibly committed. No other handler or action is modified. Evidence: handler-list screenshot, selected event identity, action editor/readback, and before/after handler comparison.

FX_RefreshButton Events > Primary is committed to FX_ImportPicture, replacing its previous FX_Test Primary assignment. The authoritative component Events property shows the exact new value. FX_Test remains present with both original actions unchanged. Evidence: button identity and Primary readback, handler inventory, two-action FX_Test readback, and pre-Save comparison.

Before Save, a complete comparison establishes only the five intended transformations: FX_VarTestEdit deletion, FX_RefreshButton caption/string change, FX_PictureStatic addition and binding, FX_ImportPicture handler creation, and FX_RefreshButton Primary reassignment. All other recorded Form components, variable definitions, handler groups, bindings, geometry, and readable attributes match the baseline, except any explicitly justified permitted button movement. Evidence: pre-Save component and handler matrices, screenshots, and mutation audit.

Exactly one ordinary Designer Save is invoked after all configuration gates pass. The native response is captured verbatim and indicates no unresolved error or unexpected confirmation. Designer Save becomes disabled, and all five intended changes remain visible in the clean post-Save definition. No regeneration or additional Save occurs. Evidence: pre-Save state, Save response, settled Designer screenshot, post-Save property readbacks, and exact Save count.

The clean FX_Items Designer Form is closed once without an unsaved-changes prompt and reopened through an approved native route. The recovered version has the identical User-scope Name, ScopeType, and ScopeName. Every intended deletion, caption/string, Static binding and No Colon value, Binary Value Action handler, and Primary event assignment is recovered. FX_VarTest, FX_Test with two actions, and all other baseline components remain unchanged. Designer Save is disabled. Evidence: close/reopen screenshots, reopened scope identity, complete recovered component and handler inventories, field-by-field comparisons, and action audit.

The FX_Items runtime Form opens read-only once and displays the three pre-existing dumbbell, eggs, and guitar records with their documented readable fields. A visible Import button and empty picture Static are present. No import or unexpected prompt is activated; no business record is modified; runtime Save remains disabled. Evidence: runtime Form identity, three-record grid/count, button and Static screenshot, clean-state readback, and runtime action audit.

The final EXP-062 report provides decisive evidence references for AC-1 through AC-11, exact component and handler baseline/recovery comparisons, FX_sImport creation evidence, the complete controlled action audit, worker-written-file inventory, any browser-tool-generated file limitations, and the final Designer/runtime state. It confirms one Designer Save, the permitted component/string/handler operations, one ordinary close/reopen, and zero runtime imports, business-record changes, checkout-management actions, or unauthorized operations. Repository confinement is supported by worker/harness inventories, with operator git review authoritative. Findings are classified observed only, without independent durability, cache, or picture-import claims.

initial_instruction: T1 — Read-only preflight and complete FX_Items Form baseline for EXP-062. Review AGENTS.md, hello-world-pt4.md Section 4 (03:00–05:13), and the related experiment evidence. Record the starting repository state using the permitted documentation and available harness evidence, without shell/git access. Confirm the operator-prepared authenticated Designer session is usable, that the loaded Form is exactly FX_Items in User scope for the authenticated operator, and that Designer Save is disabled. Do not authenticate or change sessions. Through supported native read-only controls, capture the full component inventory and relevant properties, especially FX_VarTestEdit, FX_RefreshButton, and all input fields and their geometry. Verify the FX_VarTest variable, FX_Test handler group and its two existing actions, and the absence of FX_ImportPicture. Inspect the existing FX_Picture property-binding prerequisite through a supported native selection/read-only surface without committing any change. Determine whether FX_sImport already exists without creating or editing it. Capture clear screenshots and accessibility readbacks under evidence/EXP-062/ and create the EXP-062 experiment record with a complete pre-mutation comparison baseline, action audit, limits, and worker-written-file inventory. Stop before any component deletion, string creation, Toolbox placement, handler creation, property edit, or Save. If the User-scope Form identity or any required prerequisite cannot be established, report a blocker rather than changing another version or expanding the procedure.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261011-223208-4y9y. Rationale: EXP-061 accepted the creation and same-session recovery of the FX_Picture Bound IDO property. The next tutorial step is to connect that property to the existing FX_Items Form and configure the picture-import user interface. The operator has authorized the exact Section 4 transformation: remove the obsolete variable-bound Edit component, repurpose the existing refresh button, create its Import caption string, add a picture-bound Static component, create one Binary Value Action handler, and connect the button to that handler. Treat these as one bounded Form-definition transformation with one Designer Save and one close/reopen verification. EXP-045 provides the string creation procedure, EXP-054-R2 and EXP-058 provide lessons about event-assignment verification, and EXP-061 establishes the picture-property prerequisite. All results remain observed only until independently replayed. | Operator review 2026-10-11: the import-trigger pattern now matches only clicking/pressing the Import button (a description of Primary = FX_ImportPicture no longer matches); exact_values FX_Items, FX_sImport, Import, FX_PictureStatic, FX_ImportPicture, FX_Picture (case-sensitive typing guard); deny_browser_javascript; User editing scope. Operator decisions 2026-10-11: follow the tutorial (delete FX_VarTestEdit, repurpose FX_RefreshButton); images for section 5 will be supplied by the operator later. Approved by the operator 2026-10-11 with precondition attestation: logged in, configuration OK, Web Client loaded, no unsaved changes.
